review: Partly disagree. ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: ਜਪੈ is third person singular (glossary: chants), ਜਾਪੁ is its object, and ਜਪੁ is the imperative. 'says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone' drops the third-person clause. It also differs from the writer's own treatment of the third-person verbs ਬੋਲੈ (a03.p4) and ਕਹੈ (a06.p5), which the writer renders 'Nanak utters …', 'Nanak speaks …' and uses to correct our Hindi. The owner should choose one treatment for all three.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "a06.p7", "issue": "ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: ਜਪੈ is 3rd person singular (Nanak chants the chant), ਜਪੁ imperative, ਸੋਇ 'that very One'. Same question as ਬੋਲੈ (a03.p4) and ਕਹੈ (a06.p5): indicative 'Nanak repeats' or hortative 'let one repeat'.", "our reading": "By whose grace all are liberated, Nanak repeats his Name; repeat the Name of that very One.", "alternatives": "says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone (writer; our Hindi 'हे नानक! उसीका जाप जपो'); hortative throughout: 'let one repeat …' here, and likewise in a03.p4 and a06.p5"}

review: Agree with the writer's doubt (ਸਿਮਰਨਿ is instrumental/locative, and the agent of the perfect participles ਧਾਰੀ and ਕੀਓ; 'for the sake of' has no basis in the form). Supplying 'the sages' for ਉਪਾਏ is a fair implied agent. One more line needs recording: ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਕਾਰਨ ਕਰਨਾ is rendered as an imperative, but every other line of the pauri states what Simran has done. ਸਿਮਰਿ can also be the conjunctive participle ('by remembering again and again'), and some commentaries read the line that way.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "a01.p8", "issue": "ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਕਾਰਨ ਕਰਨਾ: imperative (remember, remember the Lord) or conjunctive participle in a pauri of statements (by remembering again and again, one becomes one with the Lord, the Cause of causes)?", "our reading": "Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes (as our Hindi, which adds हे मन).", "alternatives": "Remembering him again and again, one becomes one with the Lord, the Maker of all causes (the participle reading; 'becomes one with' is implied, not in the words)."}

issue: ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੈ ਮਨਿ ਬਿਸ੍ਰਾਮ: does the Naam rest (abide) in the devotees' minds, or do the devotees' minds find rest in it? Also: the marker ਰਹਾਉ is left out of the English, like a verse number.
our reading: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Naam, the nectar of peace; it rests in the minds of the devotees. (No 'Pause'.)
alternatives: '… in it the minds of the devotees find rest' (our Hindi gives both; Sant Singh Khalsa: the minds of the devotees abide in peace). If the exporter does not add ਰਹਾਉ, end with 'Pause.'

issue: ਬੇਦ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਸੁਧਾਖੵਰ ॥ ਕੀਨੇ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਇਕ ਆਖੵਰ: were the scriptures made from the one word of the Name, or did the scriptures declare that one word the purest of words?
our reading: The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, pure words all, were made from the one word of the Lord's Name (as our Hindi).
alternatives: The Vedas, Puranas and Simritis have made (declared) the one word of the Lord's Name the purest of words.

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੈ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ
our reading: whatever happens is good (as our Hindi)
alternatives: one becomes good (Sant Singh Khalsa); whatever happens seems good to one

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕਉ ਸਿਮਰਹਿ ਸਦਾ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ has no ਸੇ, so ਸਦਾ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ could describe God.
our reading: All who remember God become forever imperishable (as our Hindi).
alternatives: They remember God, the ever-imperishable.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਧਾਰੀ ਸਭ ਧਰਨਾ and ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਕੀਓ ਸਗਲ ਅਕਾਰਾ: our Hindi reads 'for the sake of Simran' (के लिये), but ਸਿਮਰਨਿ is instrumental/locative (by, through, in). Also ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਲਗਿ ਬੇਦ ਉਪਾਏ has no subject; 'the sages' is supplied.
our reading: Through Simran of the Lord the whole earth is upheld; through Simran of the Lord all visible creation was made; absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas.
alternatives: For the sake of Simran the earth was established and creation made (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); 'the Vedas were composed' without naming who.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਾਥ: a prayer (be with Nanak) or a vocative (O God, Nanak's companion)?
our reading: I have come to your refuge; O God, stay with Nanak (as our Hindi).
alternatives: O God, ever with Nanak, I have come to your refuge.

issue: ਲਾਖ ਕਰੋਰੀ ਬੰਧੁ ਨ ਪਰੈ: object of ਬੰਧੁ is implied.
our reading: Gathering hundreds of thousands and millions, one sets no bound to craving (as our Hindi).
alternatives: One with lakhs and crores is not freed of bondage (ਬੰਧੁ as bond).

issue: Our Hindi renders ਅਸ੍ਵ ਹੈਵਰ as घोड़े, हाथी; ਹੈਵਰ (Skt. hayavara) is the finest horse, elephants being ਗੈਵਰ (gajavara). Our glossary already has 'fine horses, steeds'.
our reading: gold, horses, the finest steeds and land
alternatives: gold, horses, elephants and land (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa)

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਬੋਲੈ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ: ਬੋਲੈ is third person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (बोलो).
our reading: Nanak utters it in natural poise and with love.
alternatives: Speak it with natural ease (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); whoever utters it in poise and love (is freed of pain).

issue: ਬਿਖੋਟਿ is uncommon: what is lost?
our reading: he throws away his good faith (his trust and credit), as our Hindi
alternatives: he loses (God's favour) through faithlessness

issue: ਜੋ ਤੁਮ ਭਾਨੇ ਤਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਜਾਤਾ: ਪ੍ਰਭੁ is nominative/accusative, not vocative; our Hindi has 'तुम्हें जाना'.
our reading: Those who please you have known God.
alternatives: Those who please you, O God, have known you.

issue: ਕਰਉ ਬੇਨਤੀ: ਕਰਉ is first person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (विनती करो).
our reading: I offer my prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything.
alternatives: Offer your prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa).

issue: Is ਬਿਨਸਿ ਜਾਇ a wish, or a statement that the vices perish in God's refuge?
our reading: May lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism be destroyed. Nanak seeks the refuge of God: O divine Guru, grant your grace (as our Hindi).
alternatives: In God's refuge lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism are destroyed; O divine Guru, grant your grace (that Nanak may reach it).

issue: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਸੁ ਕਹੈ: ਕਹੈ is third person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (कह).
our reading: by the Guru's grace Nanak speaks his praise
alternatives: by the Guru's grace, speak his praise (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); by the Guru's grace one speaks his praise

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: grammar of the cognate repetition is loose.
our reading: says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone (ਸੋਇ = that very one)
alternatives: Nanak repeats that very chant; meditate and chant his chant (Sant Singh Khalsa)

issue: ਮਃ ੫ is rendered 'the Fifth Guru'; our Hindi also names Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
our reading: Sukhmani, in Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru.
alternatives: … by the Fifth Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji; or keep 'Mehla 5'.

review: I do not agree that our Hindi is wrong here. ਨਾਨਕ has no aunkar, so it is vocative (the subject form is ਨਾਨਕੁ, as in a07.salok ਨਾਨਕੁ ਬਿਨਵੰਤਾ), and ਕਹੈ continues the subject of the whole pauri, the being (ਜਿਉ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਰਾਖੈ ਤਿਵ ਹੀ ਰਹੈ); our Hindi (हे नानक! गुरुकी कृपासे (वह) सच कहता है) has this. No Hindi change; the English should follow it. ਸਚੁ may also be the True One (one speaks of the True One); owner to decide. Note batch 01 a06.p5 (ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਸੁ ਕਹੈ) has the same pattern and should be made consistent.
reviewer_fix: Sometimes one dances in many ways. Sometimes one stays asleep day and night. Sometimes one is fearsome in great anger. Sometimes one becomes the dust under everyone's feet. Sometimes one sits as a great king. Sometimes one wears the guise of a lowly beggar. Sometimes one falls into ill repute. Sometimes one is called good, very good. As God keeps one, so one remains. By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, one speaks the truth.

issue: Format: our Hindi renders the headers ਸਲੋਕੁ ॥ and ਅਸਟਪਦੀ ॥ as सलोक। / अष्टपदी।; the English keeps them as Salok. / Ashtapadi. at the start of the meaning.
our reading: Salok. / Ashtapadi. kept, to match our Hindi
alternatives: Drop the headers from the English if the other batches or the exporter handle them separately

issue: ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਸਭੁ ਹੋਤ ਨਿਬੇਰਾ: what is settled.
our reading: every conflict is settled (as our Hindi: झगड़े निपट जाते हैं)
alternatives: all one's accounts (of deeds) are settled; everything is resolved

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਧ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਬਨਿ ਆਈ: whether the Saadh and God become one, or a bond of love is formed between them.
our reading: the Saadh and God are at one
alternatives: a deep bond of love has formed between the Saadh and God; the Saadh and God have become one (our Hindi)

issue: ਸਾਧ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਕੇਵਲ ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ: the line has no verb.
our reading: one's attention rests on the Supreme Lord alone (our Hindi: केवल पारब्रह्म (का ध्यान) रहता है)
alternatives: one dwells with the Supreme Lord alone; only the Supreme Lord is seen everywhere

issue: ਸਾਧ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਸੋਭਾ ਸੁਰਦੇਵਾ: whose glory.
our reading: the gods sing one's praise (our Hindi)
alternatives: one is honoured as the gods are; one gains glory among the gods

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਧਰੈ ਸਾਧ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਸੈ: ਰਸੈ as a verb (delights) or as ਰਸਨਾ (from the tongue).
our reading: one is saved by hearing the Saadh's words and delighting in them (our Hindi and glossary)
alternatives: one is saved by hearing (the Naam) from the tongue of the Saadh (Prof. Sahib Singh's reading of ਰਸੈ as ਰਸਨਾ ਤੋਂ)

issue: ਸੁਨਉ / ਗਾਉ: the -ਉ ending of ਸੁਨਉ is first person singular (I hear), and lines 7–8 are first person plural (ਭਏ, ਹਮਾਰੀ); our Hindi reads both as commands (सुनो, गाओ).
our reading: In the Saadh's company, I hear the Lord's Name; I sing the Lord's praises
alternatives: listen to the Lord's Name; sing the Lord's praises (imperative, as our Hindi); may I hear / may I sing (wish)

issue: ਜੈਸੇ ਸੂਰੁ ਸਰਬ ਕਉ ਸੋਖ: what the simile of the sun shows; the verse gives only that the sun dries up all.
our reading: as the sun dries up all things yet stays untainted (our Hindi: सोखता है, फिर भी दोषसे अछूता)
alternatives: as the sun gives warmth to all; as the sun burns away all impurity

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਿਉ ਪਾਵਕ ਕਾ ਸਹਜ ਸੁਭਾਉ: the verse does not say which nature of fire is meant.
our reading: like the innate nature of fire (left as the verse says it)
alternatives: to give warmth to all alike (our Hindi); to burn away every impurity, purifying all it touches

issue: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ: what is good.
our reading: to the Brahm Giani, whatever happens is good (our Hindi)
alternatives: whatever comes from the Brahm Giani is good; the Brahm Giani acts for the good of all

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਪੈ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ: whom the world remembers.
our reading: by means of the Brahm Giani the whole world remembers God (our Hindi)
alternatives: the whole world remembers and praises the Brahm Giani; the Brahm Giani meditates (on God) for the whole world

issue: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਉ ਖੋਜਹਿ ਮਹੇਸੁਰ: ਖੋਜਹਿ is plural; ਮਹੇਸੁਰ may be Shiva (honorific plural) or great gods in general.
our reading: sought even by Shiva, the great lord (our Hindi: महेश्वर (शिव))
alternatives: sought by the great gods (maheshvars) such as Shiva

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਆਪਿ ਪਰਮੇਸੁਰ (also a08.p8: creator of the world, himself the Formless Lord): our Hindi adds a qualifier, (का रूप), and the English keeps the verse's own words without it.
our reading: the Brahm Giani is himself the Supreme God; is himself the Formless Lord
alternatives: add a qualifier: is a form of the Supreme God, is one with the Formless Lord

issue: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਸਗਲ ਮਨ ਮਾਹਿ: what is in the mind.
our reading: the Brahm Giani holds everything within his mind (our Hindi)
alternatives: all (virtues) are in the Brahm Giani's mind; the Brahm Giani holds all beings in his heart; the Brahm Giani is within all minds

issue: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਜੁਗਤਿ ਜੀਅ ਕਾ ਦਾਤਾ: how the three nouns go together.
our reading: gives souls the way to liberation (our Hindi)
alternatives: gives liberation, the way of life, and the soul (life) itself; gives the soul spiritual life and the way to liberation

issue: ਅਪਰਸੁ: the word names an ascetic who touches nothing for ritual purity; the stanza gives it a new sense.
our reading: the Apras, the one untouched by evil (gloss)
alternatives: the true touch-nothing; one untouched by vice and by Maya

issue: ਭਗਉਤੀ: the term may mean a worshipper of the goddess Bhagauti (Durga) or of Bhagwan; the stanza defines it as devotion to Bhagwant, the Lord.
our reading: A Bhagauti, a worshipper of the Lord, is one imbued with love for devotion to the Lord
alternatives: the true Bhagauti, devotee of the goddess, is (rather) one who loves devotion to the Lord

issue: ਪਸੁ ਪ੍ਰੇਤ ਮੁਘਦ ਪਾਥਰ: whether ਪਾਥਰ means stones or stone-hearted people.
our reading: the stone-hearted (our Hindi: पत्थर-हृदय)
alternatives: even stones

issue: ਸਦਾ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਾਨੁ: ਜਾਨੁ may be descriptive (knows) or imperative (know).
our reading: He knows the Lord to be ever near (our Hindi)
alternatives: know the Lord to be ever near (addressed to the reader)

issue: ਤੈਸਾ ਮਾਨੁ ਤੈਸਾ ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ: ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ is literally pride; set against ਮਾਨੁ (honour) it is read as the arrogance or scorn of others towards him.
our reading: Honour is the same as scorn (our Hindi: मान … अपमान)
alternatives: honour shown to him and others' arrogance towards him are the same; honour and pride are the same to him

issue: ਕਈ ਕੋਟਿ ਕੀਏ ਰਤਨ ਸਮੁਦ: two nouns, or one compound.
our reading: the jewels and oceans he has made (our Hindi)
alternatives: the jewels of the oceans; oceans of jewels

issue: ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਏਕੁ ਹੈ: ਕਰਣ may be the created world (ਕਰਣ = creation) or the doer.
our reading: The One God is the cause of all creation
alternatives: God alone is the Doer and the Cause; God alone does and causes all to be done (our Hindi)

issue: ਦੁਹਾ ਸਿਰਿਆ ਕਾ ਆਪਿ ਸੁਆਮੀ: which two ends.
our reading: Master of this world and the next (our Hindi: दोनों लोकोंका)
alternatives: Master of both sides: of Maya and of devotion, of the Gurmukh and the manmukh, of good and evil

issue: Who is the subject of the ਕਬਹੂ lines in a11.p5–p7: the helpless being (ਬਪੁਰਾ ਜੀਉ) that God moves, or God himself taking every form.
our reading: the being (rendered one), moved by God, as our Hindi
alternatives: God himself sometimes dwells high, sometimes low, plays every part

issue: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚੁ ਕਹੈ: ਨਾਨਕ as subject or vocative; ਸਚੁ as the truth or the True One.
our reading: By the Guru's grace, Nanak speaks the truth
alternatives: O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (the being) speaks the truth / utters the True One (our Hindi); by the Guru's grace the truth is told

issue: ਸਚੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਭੁ ਕੀਨਾ: whether the Maker or what he made is called true.
our reading: True, true, true is he who made everything (our Hindi)
alternatives: true, true, true is all that he has made

issue: ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਪੁਨੀਤ / ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪੈ ਨਾਨਕ ਮਨਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ: ਜਪੈ is third person, but our Hindi reads it as a command (मनमें प्रीति रखकर नाम जपो).
our reading: Holy, holy, holy and pure is the one who, O Nanak, meditates on the Naam with love in the mind
alternatives: Holy … and pure (God / his Word); Nanak meditates on the Naam with love in his mind; meditate on the Naam with love, O Nanak (our Hindi)

issue: ਸੰਤ ਕੇ ਹਤੇ ਕਉ ਰਖੈ ਨ ਕੋਇ: who is ਹਤੇ (struck down)?
our reading: No one can protect one whom a Sant has cast off (with our Hindi: ठुकराये हुए).
alternatives: One cursed by a Sant cannot be saved; no one can protect one who has wounded a Sant.

issue: ਥਾਨ ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ ਹੋਇ: ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ (masc. sg.) seems to agree with the slanderer, ਥਾਨ-ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ as a compound.
our reading: one falls from one's place (loses one's station)
alternatives: one's place becomes defiled (our Hindi: स्थान भ्रष्ट हो जाता है)

issue: ਮੁਖੁ ਭਵੈ: sense of ਭਵਣਾ.
our reading: one's face becomes twisted (our Hindi: टेढ़ा)
alternatives: one's face is turned away (from God); one's face is disgraced

issue: ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਛਲੈ: who deceives whom?
our reading: one deceives everyone (our Hindi)
alternatives: one is deceived by everyone

issue: ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਦੋਖਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ ਕੋਇ ॥ ਜੈਸਾ ਭਾਵੈ ਤੈਸਾ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਇ: sense of ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ and subject of ਭਾਵੈ.
our reading: By maligning a Sant, no one is ever satisfied. As it pleases the Lord, so a person becomes.
alternatives: ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ from tiṣṭh-: no one stands firm / survives by maligning a Sant; ਜੈਸਾ ਭਾਵੈ: as one desires (one's inclination), so one becomes.

issue: ਨਿਰਮਲ ਰਸਨਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਪੀਉ: construction.
our reading: With a pure tongue drink the nectar (our Hindi).
alternatives: Drink the nectar, and your tongue becomes pure.

issue: ਜਬ ਦੇਖਉ ਤਬ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਮੂਲੁ.
our reading: Whenever I look, everything I see is the Root, the source of all.
alternatives: Wherever I look, I see him at the root of all things.

issue: ਉਨ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੋਈ ਲਾਗੈ ॥ ਜਿਸ ਨੋ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਹਿ ਬਡਭਾਗੈ: subject of plural ਕਰਹਿ. Our Hindi takes God (honorific); the plural verb and ਉਨ (the servants) in the line before point to the servants.
our reading: He alone comes to serve them, the fortunate one on whom they (the servants) bestow grace.
alternatives: on whom God bestows grace, by great fortune (our Hindi)

issue: ਓਇ ਸੁਖ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਉਨਹੂ ਬਨਿ ਆਏ: ਓਇ is plural (they). Our Hindi reads वह सुखका खजाना है, और सेवक भी वैसे ही बन गये, which seems not to fit ਓਇ.
our reading: They become treasures of peace; this state befits them alone.
alternatives: He is the treasure of peace, and his servants become the same (our Hindi).

issue: ਸਾਚੀ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਸਾਚਾ ਆਕਾਰੁ ॥ ਸਚੁ ਵਰਤੈ ਸਾਚਾ ਪਾਸਾਰੁ: ਵਰਤੈ read as intransitive (prevails) and ਆਕਾਰੁ / ਪਾਸਾਰੁ as what the devotee sees.
our reading: His vision is true, and to him all form is true; truth prevails, and true is the whole expanse.
alternatives: His form is true; he practises truth and spreads truth (our Hindi: सच बरतता है, सच ही फैलाता है).

issue: ਸਤਿ ਕਰਮੁ: ਕਰਮੁ is both deed and grace (glossary has both).
our reading: True is his grace (ਕਰਤੂਤਿ and ਕਰਣੀ already cover deeds and doing in the same pauri).
alternatives: True are his actions (our Hindi: कर्म).

issue: ਬਿਸ੍ਵਾਸੁ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰ ਤੇ ਪਾਈ: Nanak as subject or vocative.
our reading: Nanak, true faith is received from the Guru.
alternatives: Nanak has received true faith from the Guru (our Hindi).

issue: ਅਵਰ ਨ ਬੂਝਿ ਕਰਤ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ.
our reading: No one else understands it or gives thought to it.
alternatives: No one else understands him, though they reflect (our Hindi); he himself, not another, takes thought for it.

issue: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਗਤਿ ਮਿਤਿ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਲਾਖੈ: whose state and extent? The following lines speak of the servant.
our reading: No one can perceive that servant's state and stature.
alternatives: No one can perceive God's state and extent.

issue: ਤਿਸ ਕੀ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਕਉਨ ਬਖਾਨਉ ॥ ਤਿਸ ਕਾ ਗੁਨੁ ਕਹਿ ਏਕ ਨ ਜਾਨਉ: whose glory? (also singular ਜਾਨੈ, ਪਛਾਨੈ among plural ਕਰਹਿ, ਰਹਹਿ, ਬਸਹਿ)
our reading: the glory and virtues of such a servant (with our Hindi: उनकी)
alternatives: God's glory and virtues

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਉ: imperative or means.
our reading: Nanak, sing the virtues of the Lord (with our Hindi).
alternatives: the Sikh is saved by singing the Lord's virtues.

issue: ਬੀਸ ਬਿਸਵੇ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨੈ: ਮਨੁ as object or subject.
our reading: One who accepts the Guru's will wholly, in full measure (with our Hindi).
alternatives: One with whom the Guru's mind is wholly pleased.

issue: ਸਚੁ ਉਪਦੇਸੁ ਸੇਵਕ ਕਉ ਦੇਇ: subject. The lines before and after have one subject, the person in whose mind the treasure of virtues is revealed (the Guru of this ashtapadi); our Hindi inserts प्रभु.
our reading: He (that person) gives true teaching to his servant.
alternatives: The Lord gives true teaching to his servant (our Hindi).

issue: ਜਿਸ ਕਾ ਸਾ ਤਿਨਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧਾਰੀ ॥ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਜਪਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਮੁਰਾਰੀ: ਜਪਿ imperative or absolutive.
our reading: The One whose own they were has shown grace. In the Saadh Sangat, chant the Name of Murari, the Lord.
alternatives: By chanting the Name of Murari in the Saadh Sangat, stability is found (ਜਪਿ linked to the next line).

review: Writer's doubt (fire of the womb not added). Agree that the words say only ਅਗਨਿ, but disagree with leaving bare 'the fire': most readers will not know which fire is meant, style §2 allows a one-off round-bracket gloss exactly for this, our Hindi already has (गर्भकी), and the work itself says ਗਰਭ ਅਗਨਿ in a04.p1 (rendered 'the fire of the womb' in batch 01). Recommend the gloss (fix includes the addition fix above).
reviewer_fix: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste? How can he be forgotten, who recognises what we have done? How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything? How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings? How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire (of the womb)? By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this. How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison, and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes? The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear. Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God.

review: A doubt the writer did not record: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਲਇਆ is past (ਲਇਆ, word sheet: took, obtained), but the meaning turns it into a wish ('that I may repeat'), which also decides whose praise ਤਾ ਕੀ ਉਪਮਾ is. Our Hindi and Khalsa read it as the writer does, so the meaning can stay; record it for the owner.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "a20.p6", "issue": "ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਲਇਆ ॥ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਉਪਮਾ ਕਹੀ ਨ ਜਾਇ: ਲਇਆ is past; the meaning takes the line as the content of the prayer (that I may repeat the Naam) and ਤਾ ਕੀ as God's.", "our reading": "Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His (God's) praise cannot be told (with our Hindi and Khalsa).", "alternatives": "One who by the Guru's grace has repeated the Naam, his glory cannot be told; Nanak, (God) pervades all."}

issue: ਤਿਤੁ ਘਰਿ ਜਾਇ ਬਸੈ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ: who dwells where. Our Hindi makes the devotee go and live in the house where the Imperishable is.
our reading: The Imperishable Lord comes to dwell in that heart (ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ as subject; ਤਿਤੁ ਘਰਿ = the heart of the one just described), as in Sahib Singh's teeka.
alternatives: Our Hindi: (ऐसा जन) उस घरमें जा बसता है जहाँ अविनाशी है. Khalsa: You shall go to that home, and live forever.

issue: ਤਤੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ਕਹੈ ਜਨੁ ਸਾਚਾ: is ਸਾਚਾ the subject (the true devotee says this) or the predicate (one who speaks the essential reflection is true)?
our reading: The true devotee states this essential truth: whoever keeps being born and dying is unripe (line 2 is what he states).
alternatives: Our Hindi and Khalsa: one who speaks/contemplates the essence of reality is true; one who is born and dies is unripe.

issue: ਝੂਠਾ ਡੰਫੁ ਝੂਠੁ ਪਾਸਾਰੀ: ਪਾਸਾਰੀ as the display itself, or as the one who makes the display.
our reading: a false pomp, a false display (with our Hindi and the word sheet).
alternatives: Sahib Singh: ਪਾਸਾਰੀ = the one who spreads out the show, i.e. false is he who makes this display.

issue: ਜਿ ਅਗਨਿ ਮਹਿ ਰਾਖੈ: the verse says only 'in the fire'; the tradition (and our Hindi, in brackets) understands the fire of the womb.
our reading: who keeps us safe in the fire (womb not added).
alternatives: who keeps us safe in the fire of the womb.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਭਗਤੀ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਇ: ਭਗਤੀ as 'through devotion' or as 'the devotee'.
our reading: Nanak, through devotion he merges in the Naam.
alternatives: Nanak, the devotee merges in the Naam; Khalsa: Nanak is absorbed in devotional worship of the Naam.

issue: ਸਿਵ ਸਕਤਿ: gloss. Readings vary: spirit and matter, consciousness and Maya, soul and Maya.
our reading: Shiva and Shakti, spirit and matter (the word sheet's mind/matter).
alternatives: Shiva and Shakti (no gloss); consciousness and Maya.

issue: ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਗੁਪਤ: one scribe (Chitragupta, the Puranic recorder, as on the word sheet) or two (Chitra and Gupta, as Sikh usage often has it).
our reading: Chitra and Gupta, the recorders of deeds.
alternatives: Chitragupta, the recorder of deeds.

issue: ਕੋਊ ਨਰਕ ਕੋਊ ਸੁਰਗ ਬੰਛਾਵਤ: ਬੰਛਾਵਤ governs both, literally 'one longs for hell, another for heaven'.
our reading: one is bound for hell, another longs for heaven (with our Hindi and Sahib Singh).
alternatives: some are made to long for hell, some for heaven.

issue: ਸੋ ਮੂਆ ਜਿਸੁ ਮਨਹੁ ਬਿਸਾਰੈ: who forgets whom.
our reading: that one is dead whom he (God) puts out of his mind (with our Hindi and Khalsa).
alternatives: that one is dead who puts him (God) out of his mind.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਿ ਸਭ ਮੋਹੀ: whose sight, the saint's or God's.
our reading: seeing his sight, all are enchanted (his left open, as in the verse).
alternatives: seeing the sight of such a saint (Sahib Singh); seeing God's sight.

issue: ਅੰਤਰਗਤਿ ਜਿਸੁ ਆਪਿ ਜਨਾਏ: sense of ਅੰਤਰਗਤਿ.
our reading: One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within.
alternatives: One to whom he grants the inner state (of realisation); our Hindi: to whom he makes known that he is the inner knower.

issue: Who has worshipped and found the Perfect One: the verse names no subject. Our Hindi and Khalsa use 'I'; Sahib Singh 'whoever'.
our reading: Passive: The perfect God has been worshipped …; the Perfect One has been found; sing the praises of the Perfect One.
alternatives: I have worshipped … I have found the Perfect One; I sing (Khalsa takes ਗਾਉ as first person) / sing (imperative, our Hindi).

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਧਰੇ ਤਿਨ ਕੈ ਸਾਥੇ: who is saved.
our reading: Nanak, in their company people are saved (plural ਉਧਰੇ, with our Hindi).
alternatives: Nanak is saved in their company (Khalsa).

issue: ਸੁਨਿ ਸੁਨਿ ਅਨਦ ਕਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਗਾਜੈ: 'within him' is supplied to make ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਗਾਜੈ clear.
our reading: hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him.
alternatives: he rejoices, proclaiming God's praises (Khalsa).

issue: ਸੁਖਮਨੀ ਸਹਜ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਗੁਨ ਨਾਮ: how the four nouns relate.
our reading: The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam.
alternatives: The Sukhmani gives poise; in it are Gobind's praises and the Naam (Sahib Singh-style).

issue: ਹਰਿ ਧਨੁ ਖਾਟਿ ਚਲੈ ਜਨੁ ਸੋਇ ॥ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਿਸਹਿ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ: what is 'granted'.
our reading: That servant departs having earned the wealth of the Lord, Nanak, who is granted it (it = this wealth / the Sukhmani).
alternatives: Khalsa: One who departs after earning the wealth of the Lord's Name realises it.

issue: ਇਹ ਫਲ ਤਿਸੁ ਜਨ ਕੈ ਮੁਖਿ ਭਨੇ ॥ ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮ ਬਚਨ ਮਨਿ ਸੁਨੇ: ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ is in the text; the brief's rule is to write Nanak, not Guru Nanak, for the signature.
our reading: these fruits come to that servant who speaks the Naam with his mouth, and with his mind hears the word of the Naam from Guru Nanak (ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ kept as the text has it).
alternatives: … who, Nanak, hears with his mind the Guru's word of the Naam (ਗੁਰ with ਬਚਨ, ਨਾਨਕ as signature); or: these fruits are said to be in the mouth of that servant.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ without aunkar (no ੁ) is, by the grammar of Sahib Singh's school, an address ("O Nanak") rather than the subject (ਨਾਨਕੁ). The final pass applied this to every last line; it was reverted in these eight, where our Hindi, the reviewers and the common understanding read Nanak as the subject.
our reading: Nanak as the subject in these eight; "O Nanak" kept in a06.p7, a11.p6 and a19.p4, where our Hindi already reads the address
alternatives: apply the address reading to every bare ਨਾਨਕ, in Hindi and English alike
